1:1.idea: Complex outlines can be made from familiar shapes.
steps: Look at the outline, not the decoration.
Find the simple shapes that make it up.
Check the shapes cover the whole outline.
1:1.tip: Decoration like colour doesn't change the shapes.

1:2.idea: Build an outline by choosing and arranging shapes.
1:2.example: Rocket → rectangle body, triangle nose, 2 triangle fins
steps: Look at the outline you need to make.
Choose shapes that fit each part.
Arrange them to match the whole outline.

1:3.idea: The same outline can be built in more than one way.
steps: Keep the outer outline the same.
Try different shapes inside it.
Check every design condition still holds.

2:1.idea: Combine solids to build an object, keeping every part supported.
2:1.example: Crane → cylinder base, rectangular prism arm
steps: Choose solids for each part.
Place them so raised parts rest on something.
Check the build matches the brief.
2:1.tip: Nothing can float in the air.

2:2.idea: One view can hide structure, so use every view.
2:2.example: Front view shows heights; top view shows positions
steps: Read the front and side views for heights.
Read the top view for positions.
Build stacks that match all views together.
2:2.tip: A build must match every view, not just one.

2:3.idea: Some cubes can't be seen, but they must be there for support.
2:3.example: A cube on the second layer needs a cube under it
steps: Look at the visible cubes.
Check which ones need support below or behind.
Add the fewest hidden cubes needed.
2:3.tip: Every raised cube needs one underneath.

3:1.idea: A simple version keeps the features that make an object recognisable.
3:1.example: Tree icon → triangle top + rectangle trunk
steps: Decide which features identify the object.
Use simple shapes for those features.
Leave out extra details.
3:1.tip: Keep the parts that show what it is.

3:2.idea: Build a model that matches its purpose.
3:2.example: Robot: square head, rectangle body, 2 arms
steps: Read the brief: what must be shown?
Build with the shapes available.
Check that someone could recognise it.
3:2.tip: Revise if it could be confused with something else.

3:3.idea: Judge which model is better by checking the brief.
3:3.example: House A is missing its door → House B is complete
steps: List what the brief requires.
Check each model against the list.
Choose the model that meets every requirement.

4:1.idea: A grid reference names one cell: column letter, then row number.
steps: Find the column letter along the bottom or top.
Find the row number along the side.
The cell where they meet is the reference.

4:2.idea: Use grid references to find, report or place features.
4:2.example: Which landmark is at D3? → find column D, row 3
steps: Read the reference.
Find the column, then the row.
Read the landmark in that cell.
4:2.tip: The reference names the cell, not a line.

4:3.idea: A grid system labels every column and row in order.
4:3.example: Columns A, B, C, D… rows 1, 2, 3, 4…
steps: Label the columns with letters in order.
Label the rows with numbers in order.
Check nothing is missing or repeated.
4:3.tip: Every cell must have one unique reference.

5:1.idea: A route moves from one grid reference to another.
5:1.example: From B2, move 3 right and 1 up → E3
steps: Start at the first reference.
Apply each move: right changes the letter, up changes the number.
Record the reference reached.

5:2.idea: Write directions someone else can follow exactly.
steps: Write each move with a direction and number of cells.
Run the route on the grid.
Fix it if it misses the goal.
5:2.tip: Each move needs a direction and a distance.

5:3.idea: A valid route must reach the goal and follow every rule.
5:3.example: Avoid closed sectors and visit the relay first
steps: List the rules.
Plan a route that follows them all.
Test it. The shortest route may not be allowed.

6:1.idea: Line symmetry means each part matches its mirror image across the line.
6:1.example: Fold along the line → both halves match
steps: Pick a feature on one side.
Find the matching spot the same distance across the line.
Check every feature matches.
6:1.tip: Balanced is not the same as symmetric.

6:2.idea: Complete a reflection by copying each tile to the opposite side.
6:2.example: Tile 2 squares left of the line → place it 2 squares right
steps: Measure each tile's distance from the line.
Place its match the same distance on the other side.
Check every tile has a match.
6:2.tip: Distance is measured straight across the line.

6:3.idea: Create a symmetric design, then test it.
6:3.example: Build any design, then mirror it across the line
steps: Place tiles on one side.
Mirror each tile across the line.
Test the whole design and fix mismatches.
6:3.tip: Test every tile, not just most.

7:1.idea: A design has rotational symmetry if it matches itself after less than a full turn.
7:1.example: After a half turn (180°) it looks the same → symmetric
steps: Turn the design around its centre.
Compare it with the start.
If it matches before a full turn, it has rotational symmetry.
7:1.tip: Every shape matches after a full turn, so that doesn't count.

7:2.idea: Record which turns make the design match.
steps: Turn the design a quarter turn.
Check if it matches.
Record the smallest turn that matches.
7:2.tip: Keep the centre fixed while turning.

7:3.idea: Create a pattern that matches after a turn.
7:3.example: Repeat a motif in each quarter around the centre
steps: Place a motif.
Copy it, turned, around the centre.
Test the turn and fix any mismatch.
7:3.tip: Turn the motif, don't just copy it.

8:1.idea: Break a design brief into its parts.
steps: List each condition in the brief.
Decide what evidence each one needs.
Plan an order so finished work isn't undone.

8:2.idea: Build a connected design where every condition passes.
8:2.example: Build the base, place sectors, add a symmetric signal
steps: Build each part.
Connect them as the brief says.
Check every condition.
8:2.tip: One failed condition means it's not finished.

8:3.idea: Audit a design: test each part and fix the first failure.
8:3.example: Replay the route, test the symmetry, check the build
steps: Test each subsystem from the start.
Fix the first thing that fails.
Retest until everything passes.
8:3.tip: Fix one problem at a time.
